co2_as_printed: ISS ppCO2 2.7 mm Hg at the time; readings mostly below 4, never above 6
symptoms_reported: headaches, reported months after the mission
action_or_outcome: headaches relieved by acetaminophen and by breathing oxygen in EMU suits
verbatim_quote: At the time, the ISS ppCO2 was 2.7 mm Hg, and both the ISS and Shuttle ppCO2 readings on that day were low (mostly less than 4 mm Hg and never exceeding 6 mm Hg); as a result, the LiOH was not installed.

co2_as_printed: up to 7.5 mm Hg before change out of the CDRA
symptoms_reported: headache in one Shuttle crewmember the same day
action_or_outcome: LiOH installed; no further reports after the CDRA was reactivated
verbatim_quote: A Shuttle crewmember reported headache symptoms on the same day as elevated CO2 levels up to 7.5 mm Hg were recorded before change out of the CDRA.

co2_as_printed: above 4 mm Hg, within flight rule limits; relief at about 2 mm Hg
symptoms_reported: lethargy, malaise, listlessness and fatigue, two separate reports
action_or_outcome: symptoms subsided within minutes of reducing ppCO2 to the 2 mm Hg range or breathing 100% oxygen
verbatim_quote: There were two separate reports of lethargy, malaise, listlessness, and fatigue when ppCO2 rose above 4 mm Hg but remained within flight rule limits.

action_or_outcome: EVA terminated early over a failing LiOH canister and rising CO2
verbatim_quote: On STS-127/2JA, EVA-3 was terminated early due to concern about a failing LiOH canister and rising CO2 levels. CO2 concentrations remained below flight limits and peaked at 3 mm Hg.
